name: 2S7 Pion / Malka

placement_rationale.text: 2S7 Pion/Malka's real-world range (per this asset's own Wikipedia source) runs to roughly 37 km with standard rounds and up to ~47.5 km with rocket-assisted projectiles, so 12 km draws on only about a quarter to a third of that reach — a wider margin, in absolute terms, than most of the tracked SPGs in this comparison set. That extra standoff offsets the platform's own noted limitation of being very heavy and slow to reposition: a gun that can't shoot-and-scoot needs more distance rather than more speed to survive counter-battery fire, consistent with doctrine.md §2's finding that local drone/counter-battery pressure sets standoff distance. 12 km sits inside doctrine.md's 10–150+ km medium/long-range strike layer, clear of the close-in 0–10 km FPV strike zone.

characteristics: 203mm howitzer - the largest-caliber SPG in wide use in this war
Strength: Extreme range and shell weight compared to standard 152mm/155mm systems
Limitation: Very heavy and slow to reposition; 203mm ammunition is far less abundant than standard 152mm stock
Estimated quantity available: Reserve stock reactivation; exact fielded total not disclosed
employment_notes: A Cold War heavy-artillery type reactivated from reserve stock due to wartime attrition of more modern systems - fits the same 'reactivated Soviet-era equipment' pattern documented for Russian tanks
contrast_vs_traditional: The Pion/Malka's 203mm gun was built for Cold War-scale mass artillery duels at extreme range, when a gun this large mattered more for its throw weight than its footprint. Its size is now closer to a liability than an asset — concealment and rapid displacement, the traits that matter most under persistent drone observation, are exactly what a vehicle this large struggles to do well.
